<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense peak at m/z 233.9632 likely corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈232.9559 Da. The isotopic pattern (significant M+2 peak at ~24 % intensity) indicates the presence of a single chlorine atom. Removing the monoisotopic chlorine mass (34.9689 Da) leaves ≈197.9871 Da to be accounted for by C, H, and O. The combination C₁₁H₂O₄ matches this remainder within a few ppm. Adding back the chlorine gives the molecular formula C₁₁H₂O₄Cl, which reproduces the observed m/z within acceptable error and explains the chlorine isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>C11H2O4Cl</final_answer>
